## Verdict per target

- `CpuSetup` has no RUNTIME attribute, so the running system cannot read or write it (observed in the NVAR attributes), and no authenticated-write attribute.
- **Overclocking lock** and **default power limits / thermal throttle point**: all of them live in `CpuSetup`, as ordinary one-byte or four-byte fields. A boot-time setting change (writing the field before the OS starts, from a UEFI shell tool or a setup_var-style GRUB command) can reach them, because the variable is boot-service accessible and not authenticated (inferred from the attributes; not yet tried on this board). Owners of older boards from this manufacturer report boot-time changes lasting only one boot, so the first attempt must check that the value survives a second reboot.
- **Hidden setup menus**: the forms link all top-level tabs from the root form without any condition (observed above), so whatever hides menus on the setup screen is not in the forms or in a variable this report can see. On AMI Aptio V that is the setup browser's own page and access data (AMITSE, inferred), which is code in the image, not a setting: **a modified image is required**. Which tabs the setup screen actually shows has to be confirmed by eye (unknown from the image alone).
